events.title: Writing invented in Mesopotamia
events.desc: Sumerian scribes in cities such as Uruk start pressing cuneiform signs into clay tablets, first to keep accounts.

events.title: Egypt unified under the first pharaoh
Great Pyramid of Giza completed
events.desc: Built for the pharaoh Khufu, it remains the tallest human-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.

events.title: Confucius leaves the state of Lu
Confucius returns to Lu to teach
Alexander the Great's reign
events.desc: In 13 years Alexander builds an empire from Greece to Egypt and the edge of India.

events.title: Alexander reaches India
events.desc: At the Battle of the Hydaspes, in today's Pakistan, Alexander defeats King Porus. His exhausted army then refuses to go further east.

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.desc: Qin Shi Huang becomes the first emperor of a unified China and standardises its script, coins and weights.

events.title: Paper invented
events.desc: Court official Cai Lun is credited with refining papermaking from bark, hemp and rags.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.desc: Emperors Constantine and Licinius grant religious tolerance across the Roman Empire, ending the persecution of Christians.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
Hijra: Muhammad moves to Medina
events.desc: Year one of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Charlemagne becomes King of the Franks
University of al-Qarawiyyin founded
events.desc: Founded in Fez by Fatima al-Fihri; often called the oldest university still operating.

events.title: Jelling stone raised by Harald Bluetooth
Vikings at L'Anse aux Meadows
events.desc: Norse sailors from Greenland build a camp in Newfoundland, nearly 500 years before Columbus.

events.title: Stephen I crowned King of Hungary
The Tale of Genji
events.desc: Written by the court lady Murasaki Shikibu; often called the world's first novel.

events.title: Cnut the Great becomes king of England
Battle of Hastings
events.desc: William, Duke of Normandy, defeats King Harold II and becomes the first Norman king of England.

events.title: Mongol Empire
events.desc: At its height, the largest land empire in history, stretching from Korea to Hungary.

events.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
events.desc: The king of Mali travels with so much gold that he depresses its price in Cairo for years.

events.title: Ibn Battuta's travels
events.desc: About 117,000 km in 29 years — from Morocco to China, India, East Africa and Mali, further than any traveller before the age of steam.

events.title: Black Death
events.desc: Plague spreads from Central Asia along trade routes and kills perhaps a third to half of Europe's population.

events.title: Zheng He's treasure voyages
events.desc: Seven Ming fleets, some with more than 200 ships, sail as far as East Africa — decades before Portugal reaches India.

events.title: Jan Hus burned at the stake
Joan of Arc hears her voices
Joan of Arc lifts the siege of Orléans
Joan of Arc captured at Compiègne
Joan of Arc burned at the stake
Fall of Constantinople
events.desc: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II takes the city, ending the Byzantine Empire after more than a thousand years.

events.title: Gutenberg Bible printed
events.desc: Movable-type printing in Mainz makes books cheap enough to spread ideas across Europe.

events.title: Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
Fall of Granada
events.desc: The last Muslim kingdom in Iberia surrenders to Ferdinand and Isabella, ending the Reconquista.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.desc: Sailing for Spain, Columbus lands in the Bahamas believing he has reached Asia.

events.title: Luther's 95 Theses
events.desc: Martin Luther's challenge to the Catholic Church in Wittenberg starts the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Magellan–Elcano circumnavigation
events.desc: Of five ships and about 270 men, one ship and 18 men return to Spain after the first voyage around the world.

events.title: Diet of Worms
events.desc: Ordered to recant before Emperor Charles V, Luther refuses and is declared an outlaw.

events.title: Gustav Vasa becomes king of Sweden
Atlantic slave trade
events.desc: Roughly 12.5 million Africans are forcibly shipped across the Atlantic to the Americas.

events.title: Sack of Rome by imperial troops
Eighty Years' War
events.desc: The Dutch provinces revolt against Habsburg Spain, starting with the Battle of Heiligerlee. Independence is recognised 80 years later.

events.title: Act of Abjuration
events.desc: The northern provinces formally renounce Philip II of Spain, an early declaration of independence.

events.title: Dutch East India Company (VOC) founded
events.desc: Often called the first multinational company, and the first to issue shares traded on a stock exchange.

events.title: New Amsterdam founded
events.desc: The Dutch West India Company settles the tip of Manhattan. It becomes New York in 1664.

events.title: Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems
Sakoku: Japan closes to the world
events.desc: For two centuries only Dutch and Chinese traders may trade, the Dutch confined to the island of Dejima in Nagasaki.

events.title: Tasman reaches Tasmania and New Zealand
Amsterdam's new city hall (now Royal Palace)
Newton's plague years
events.desc: Sent home from Cambridge by the plague, Newton works out calculus, his theory of colour and the first ideas of gravity.

events.title: Rampjaar — the Disaster Year
events.desc: France, England, Münster and Cologne attack the Republic at once; the De Witt brothers are lynched in The Hague.

events.title: Revocation of the Edict of Nantes
events.desc: Louis XIV outlaws Protestantism; around 200,000 Huguenots flee, many to the Dutch Republic, England and Prussia.

events.title: William of Orange lands in England
events.desc: The Glorious Revolution: the Dutch stadtholder invades and takes the English throne as William III.

events.title: Peter the Great's Grand Embassy
events.desc: Travelling half-incognito, the tsar works as a ship's carpenter in Zaandam and Amsterdam to learn Western shipbuilding.

events.title: Peter proclaimed Emperor of All Russia
Seven Years' War
events.desc: Fought on five continents; Britain takes Canada from France and becomes the leading colonial power.

events.title: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
Industrial Revolution
events.desc: Steam power, factories and railways transform Britain first, then Europe and North America.

events.title: House of Slaves built on Gorée
Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations
Treaty of Paris ends the Revolutionary War
Haitian Revolution
events.desc: Enslaved Africans overthrow French rule and found the first state born from a successful slave revolt.

events.title: Jenner's smallpox vaccine
events.desc: Edward Jenner protects a boy against smallpox with cowpox — the first vaccine.

events.title: Heiligenstadt Testament
events.desc: In a letter to his brothers, Beethoven admits he is going deaf and that he considered suicide.

events.title: Louisiana Purchase
events.desc: The US buys about 2.1 million km² from Napoleon's France for $15 million, doubling its size.

events.title: Invasion of Russia
events.desc: Napoleon's Grande Armée of about 600,000 men marches into Russia; fewer than 100,000 make it back.

events.title: Year Without a Summer
events.desc: Ash from the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora cools the planet; harvests fail across Europe and New England.

events.title: Indian removal and the Trail of Tears
First telegraph message
events.desc: "What hath God wrought" — sent by Samuel Morse from Washington to Baltimore.

events.title: Great Famine in Ireland
events.desc: Potato blight causes famine; about a million people die and another million emigrate.

events.title: Taiping Rebellion
events.desc: A civil war against the Qing that kills an estimated 20–30 million people.

events.title: Nightingale arrives at Scutari
events.desc: Her nurses clean up the army hospital; as "the Lady with the Lamp" she becomes a national hero.

events.title: On the Origin of Species
events.desc: Darwin sets out evolution by natural selection. The first print run sells out at once.

events.title: Slavery abolished in Suriname and the Antilles
German Empire proclaimed
events.desc: Wilhelm I is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.

events.title: Berlin Conference opens
events.desc: European powers meet in Berlin to set rules for dividing up Africa. No Africans are invited.

events.title: Congo Free State
events.desc: King Leopold II rules the Congo as his private property; forced labour for rubber kills millions.

events.title: Brazil abolishes slavery
events.desc: The Golden Law makes Brazil the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery.

events.title: Van Gogh cuts off his ear
Ellis Island opens
events.desc: Over the next 62 years, about 12 million immigrants pass through its halls.

events.title: New Zealand: votes for women
events.desc: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country where women can vote in national elections.

events.title: Battle of Adwa
events.desc: Ethiopia defeats an invading Italian army and keeps its independence through the Scramble for Africa.

events.title: Einstein's annus mirabilis
events.desc: Four papers in one year — the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and E = mc² — written while working as a patent clerk in Bern.

events.title: Machu Picchu brought to world attention
Nobel Prize in Chemistry
events.desc: Curie becomes the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, and still the only one in two different sciences.

events.title: Nigeria unified as a British colony
Archduke Franz Ferdinand assassinated
events.desc: The heir to Austria-Hungary's throne is shot in Sarajevo. Within six weeks Europe is at war.

events.title: Neutral in the First World War
Mobile X-ray units on the front
Battle of the Somme
events.desc: On the first day alone the British army suffers about 57,000 casualties.

events.title: US enters the First World War
Lenin arrives in Petrograd
events.desc: Germany lets him cross in a sealed train, hoping he will take Russia out of the war.

events.title: October Revolution
events.desc: Lenin's Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd (25 October in the old Russian calendar).

events.title: Spanish flu pandemic
events.desc: An influenza pandemic infects about a third of the world's population and kills tens of millions.

events.title: Kaiser Wilhelm II flees to the Netherlands
events.desc: Germany's last emperor crosses the border at Eijsden and is granted asylum. The Netherlands refuses Allied demands to hand him over; he lives at Huis Doorn until his death in 1941.

events.title: Eclipse confirms relativity
events.desc: Arthur Eddington's expedition measures starlight bending around the Sun during a solar eclipse, as relativity predicted. Einstein becomes world-famous overnight.

events.title: Insulin first used to treat diabetes
Einstein wins the Nobel Prize
events.desc: The 1921 physics prize, announced a year late, is awarded for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.

events.title: Afsluitdijk completed
events.desc: A 32 km dam closes off the Zuiderzee, turning it into the freshwater IJsselmeer.

events.title: Einstein's letter to Roosevelt
events.desc: Einstein signs a letter warning that Germany might build an atomic bomb, which helps start the US nuclear programme.

events.title: The Holocaust
events.desc: Nazi Germany systematically murders six million Jews, along with Roma, disabled people and others.

events.title: February strike
events.desc: Amsterdam workers strike against the persecution of the Jews — the first mass protest against the Nazis in occupied Europe.

events.title: Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies
In hiding in the Secret Annex
Rescue of the Danish Jews
events.desc: Danes ferry about 7,200 Jews across the Øresund to neutral Sweden in a few weeks.

events.title: Hunger Winter
events.desc: A German blockade and a harsh winter cause a famine in the occupied west; about 20,000 people die.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh declares Vietnam independent
Jackie Robinson breaks baseball's colour line
The Diary of Anne Frank published
Indian independence and Partition
events.desc: British India is split into India and Pakistan; up to 15 million people are displaced and hundreds of thousands killed.

events.title: North Sea flood
events.desc: A storm surge breaks the dikes in Zeeland and South Holland, killing 1,836 people in the Netherlands.

events.title: Kahlo's first solo show in Mexico
Churchill wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
Rosa Parks refuses to give up her seat
Ghana becomes independent
events.desc: Led by Kwame Nkrumah, the Gold Coast becomes the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence.

events.title: Great Leap Forward
events.desc: Mao's push to industrialise overnight leads to a famine in which tens of millions die.

events.title: Pelé wins his first World Cup
Valdivia earthquake
events.desc: Magnitude 9.5, the most powerful earthquake ever recorded.

events.title: "We choose to go to the Moon"
Valentina Tereshkova: first woman in space
Tanganyika and Zanzibar unite as Tanzania
King wins the Nobel Peace Prize
Canada adopts the Maple Leaf flag
Neruda wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
"Lucy" discovered
events.desc: A 3.2-million-year-old skeleton of Australopithecus afarensis, found at Hadar.

events.title: Khmer Rouge regime
events.desc: Pol Pot's regime empties the cities; an estimated 1.5–2 million Cambodians die.

events.title: Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo
Saddam Hussein becomes president of Iraq
Benazir Bhutto becomes prime minister
events.desc: The first woman elected to lead a Muslim-majority country.

events.title: World Wide Web proposed
events.desc: Tim Berners-Lee, working at CERN near Geneva, writes the proposal that becomes the Web.

events.title: Pan-European Picnic opens the Iron Curtain
Mandela wins the Nobel Peace Prize
Rwandan genocide
events.desc: In about 100 days, Hutu extremists murder an estimated 500,000–800,000 people, most of them Tutsi.

events.title: Toy Story, the first computer-animated feature
Hong Kong handed back to China
Wangari Maathai wins the Nobel Peace Prize
National Apology to the Stolen Generations
Global financial crisis
events.desc: Lehman Brothers collapses, triggering the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

events.title: Football World Cup in South Africa
Malala Yousafzai wins the Nobel Peace Prize
Gravitational waves detected
events.desc: LIGO detects ripples in spacetime from two merging black holes, a century after Einstein predicted them.

events.title: First image of a black hole
COVID-19 pandemic
events.desc: The WHO declares a pandemic on 11 March 2020 and ends the global health emergency on 5 May 2023.
